agent.description: Name of the agent definition to run, for example `reviewer`.

session_id.description:
Target session. It must use Claude Code or Codex and be in plan mode,
where the daemon denies every permission request, bans the editing and
shell tools of Claude Code and keeps Codex read-only.

text.description: The request the agent is given, after its own instructions.

BackendKind.description:
The agent backend that drives a session.

Adding a variant requires a `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump: older peers reject
unknown variants rather than ignoring them.

oneOf.description: Claude Code CLI.
Codex through its app server.
Codex through one-shot exec runs.
Anthropic API.
Any API compatible with the `OpenAI` chat format.
Scripted backend used in tests.

Capabilities.description:
Optional features a daemon offers. A flag the peer does not send reads as
false, so a client can tell an older daemon from one that has the feature.

Add a flag when a change adds events or fields and is not breaking. Bump
[`PROTOCOL_VERSION`] only for a breaking change.

A flag is daemon-wide and says the daemon can send the event or field. It
does not say every session does: today only Claude Code sessions produce
`usage`, `rate_limit` and `usage_limit` details, so a session on another
backend never sends them even when the flag is true. A client must not wait
for one.

rate_limit_events.description: The daemon can send `rate_limit` events. Only Claude Code sessions do.

tool_call_events.description:
The daemon can send `tool_call` events. Claude Code, Codex and coda's own
loop do; a backend without tool calls never does.

usage_details.description: The daemon can report the full usage of a turn, including cache tokens.

usage_limit_events.description:
The daemon can send a `usage_limit` event when a turn ends at the plan limit.
Only Claude Code sessions do.

ContextFill.description: How full the model's context is after a model call.

used_tokens.description: Tokens the last call held in its context: the input, cached or not.

window_tokens.description: The most the model's context can hold.

backends.description: The enabled backends, in the order the daemon registers them.

any_provider_enabled.description: Whether at least one backend is enabled. Absent from older daemons, which read as enabled.

client_count.description: Connections open right now, including the one asking.

ErrorObject.description: The error member of a failed [`Response`].

code.description: Error code, see the named constants in this module.

Event.description:
One event of a session.

A variant added later reads as [`Event::Unknown`] on an older peer, so
adding one does not need a `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump. The daemon announces
the matching `Capabilities` flag at `initialize`.

`Unknown` is receive-only. It keeps nothing of the original event, so it
serializes as `{"type":"unknown"}`. A client or relay must not store or
forward it as if it were the original; keep the raw JSON line instead when
the original has to survive.

oneOf.description: A permission request was approved.
A permission request was denied.
A permission request timed out without an answer.
A turn finished.

is_error.description: Whether the turn ended in an error.

oneOf.description: Token usage reported for a turn.

context.description: How full the context is, when the backend and the model's window are known.

turn_id.description: The turn the usage belongs to.

oneOf.description: Approvals cannot be answered, so risky calls are refused.
A new backend thread could not be given the conversation so far.

reason.description: Why the earlier turns are missing.

oneOf.description: A piece of streamed model text.
The backend process ended unexpectedly.

detail.description: The last lines the process wrote to its error stream, when it wrote any.

exit_code.description: Exit code, when the process exited normally enough to have one.

will_restart.description:
Whether the daemon starts the backend again for the same turn, so the
turn is still running. Absent means no restart follows.

oneOf.description: A running turn was cut short.

cause.description: Why the turn was cut short; absent in events stored before it was recorded.

oneOf.description:
The oldest messages of a conversation were replaced by a summary of them.
The summary text is kept in the session's originals, never in the event.

kept_messages.description: How many recent messages were kept as they were.

replaced_messages.description: How many of the oldest messages the summary replaced.

summary.description: Where the summary text is kept.

oneOf.description: The provider reported its rate-limit state.

The turn ended in error because the provider's plan limit was hit.
Sent just before that turn's `result`.

reset_at.description: When the window resets, in seconds since the Unix epoch, when the provider says.

oneOf.description:
A tool call started or finished. A call sends one event for each, with the
same `id`, `name` and `summary`. A turn that ends in `turn_interrupted` or
`backend_crashed` first ends its open calls as `failed`. Only the session's
own calls are reported, not those of a sub-agent it started.

id.description: The backend's id for the call; a start and its finish share it.

name.description: The tool's name as its backend calls it, such as `Bash` or `bash`.

status.description: Whether the call began, or how it ended.

summary.description: What the call works on, cut to [`MAX_TOOL_SUMMARY_CHARS`], when it has one.

turn_id.description: The turn that made the call.

oneOf.description: An event of a type this peer does not know, sent by a newer one.

GrantAddParams.description:
Parameters of [`GRANT_ADD`]. A grant matches only when repository, tool,
cwd and pattern all equal the requested call.

cwd.description: Working directory the grant applies to.

pattern.description: Exact command or argument pattern the grant covers.

repo_path.description: Canonical root of the git repository the grant applies to.

granted_at.description: When the grant was first stored, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

anyOf.description: Null identifier, used when the request id could not be determined.

capabilities.description: Optional features the daemon offers; absent from daemons that predate them.

InterruptCause.description: Why a turn was cut short.

oneOf.description: A client cancelled the turn, or the daemon is shutting down.
The backend stayed silent past a watchdog limit.
The backend process went away before the turn could finish.
The daemon stopped while the turn ran, and found it open on the next start.
The daemon is shutting down and did not start the backend again.
A cause this peer does not know, sent by a newer one.

Mode.description: How much autonomy the agent has in a session.

oneOf.description: Ask before risky actions.
Plan only, make no changes.
Apply file edits without asking.

Notification.description: A call that expects no response.

method.description: Name of the method to invoke.

OriginalId.description: Identifies a stored original tool output.

PermissionDecision.description: The answer to a permission request.

oneOf.description: Allow this one call.
Allow this call and matching calls later.
Refuse the call.

PermissionRequestParams.description:
Params of the `permission.request` notification that asks a client to
answer a tool call.

agent.description:
Name of the sub-agent that asks, absent when the session's own call
asks. A client shows it apart from `command`, which is the model's text.

command.description:
The command line, or the tool name followed by the paths it acts on
when the call has no command line.

options.description:
For a question the model asks the user (`tool` is `ask`): the choices,
in the order the answer's `choice` counts them from 0. `command` is then
the question. Empty for a tool call.

reason.description:
What the backend or its model says the call is for, cut to 500
characters. Absent when it gave nothing, as coda's own loop does. A
client shows it apart from `command` and as a claim, since the text is
not checked.

repo_path.description: Canonical root of the git repository the call runs in.

tool.description: Normalized name of the tool that asks.

choice.description:
For a question the model asked: the option picked, counted from 0. Absent
when the user declined to pick one.

no_terminal.description:
True when the client has no user to ask, as `coda run` has none. The
model is told so, instead of being told the user declined.

accepted.description: Whether the request was still pending and took the decision.

RateLimit.description:
What a provider reported about its rate limits.

The status and window names are the provider's own words, since the set can
grow without a protocol change.

is_using_overage.description: Whether the plan's usage is being billed as overage.

overage_disabled_reason.description: Why overage is unavailable, when the provider says.

overage_resets_at.description: When the overage allowance resets, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

resets_at.description: When that window resets, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

window_type.description: The window the status is about, when the provider names one.

RateLimitWindow.description: One rate-limit window of a provider plan, such as `five_hour` or `seven_day`.

name.description: The provider's name for the window.

resets_at.description: When the window resets, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

utilization_bps.description:
Share of the window used, in basis points: 900 is 9%. It is not capped, so
a window the plan has overrun reports more than 10000.

id.description: Correlates the response with this request.

method.description: Name of the method to invoke.

force.description:
Also kill the backend's process group at once, for a stop that did not
take. Only a daemon that reports `force_cancel` honors it; an older one
ignores it and cancels as usual.

cancelled.description: Whether a running turn was cancelled.

closed.description: Whether the session held a backend server or conversation that was released.

model.description: Model to use, or the backend default.

SessionInfo.description: A session as listed to clients.

model.description: Model in use, when one is selected.

cwd.description: Only sessions started in this working directory, or every session when absent.

limit.description: Most sessions to return; the daemon applies its own default and ceiling.

keep_conversation.description: Restore the files only and keep every turn in the conversation.

keep_files.description: Leave the working tree as it is and roll back the conversation only.

session_id.description: Session to rewind. It must have no turn running.

turn_id.description:
The turn to go back to: the files return to how this turn left them and
the turns after it are rolled back. Omit it to go back to before the
first turn.

files_restored.description: Whether the working tree was restored.

saved_as.description:
The private git ref that holds the files as they were just before the
restore, so work made since the last turn can be brought back with
`git restore --source <ref>`. Absent when the files were not restored.

turns_rolled_back.description:
How many turns were newly rolled back. They stay stored and shown, and the
conversation the backend is given leaves them out.

max_turns.description: Most agent turns the session's loop may take, when it is built for this send.

token_cap.description: Most tokens the session's loop may spend, when it is built for this send.

SessionStatus.description: Whether a session has a turn running.

oneOf.description: No turn is running.
A turn is starting or running.

since_seq.description: Replay events after this sequence number, or only new events.

SessionSummary.description: Metadata of one stored session; never its content.

created_at.description: Creation time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

updated_at.description: Time of the last event, or the creation time when there is none.

TokenUsage.description: Token counts for a turn or a whole session.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens served from the prompt cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

oneOf.description: The call began and has no result yet.
The call finished and the tool reported no error.
The call finished with an error, or was denied.
A status this peer does not know, sent by a newer one.

TurnId.description: Identifies one turn within a session.

session_id.description: Session to summarize, or every session when absent.

saved_bytes.description: Bytes of tool output the token economy kept out of the context.

usage.description: Total usage of the summarized sessions.

UsageWindowKind.description: Which plan window a usage limit belongs to.

oneOf.description: The rolling five-hour window.
The rolling seven-day window.
A window that counts one model only, such as the seven-day Opus window.
A monthly window.

A window this peer does not know, sent by a newer one. Also any name the
provider reports that has no kind of its own, such as `overage`.
